MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  (MARLOMA SEWER WORKSHOP)
  DECEMBER 10, 2019

An adjourned meeting of the Rolling Hills Estates City Council was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 6:05 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City
Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development & Public Works David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

Willdan Staff:  Tyrone Peter, Deputy Director
  Ron Stein, Project Manager
  Mike Medve, Finance Manager

3.  WORKSHOP DISCUSSION ITEM

A.  MARLOMA NEIGHBORHOOD -- SEPTIC TO SEWER PUBLIC WORKS
  PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct a workshop to discuss the
  feasibility of establishing a sewer assessment district for the Marloma
  neighborhood and direct staff accordingly.

  Community Development/Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report
  (as per the agenda material) including a general overview of the process and
  three options for moving the project forward, including the costs associated with
  each of the three options shown below:

  OPTION 1  OPTION 2  OPTION 3
  Initial Cost  $180,000  $690,000  $45,000
  Risk Level  Moderate  Lowest  Highest
  Risk Contingency  5%  0%  10%
  Bond Amount  $5,105,000  $4,625,000  $5,305,000
  Annual Assessment / unit  $5,454  $6,002  $6,230
  Prepaid Assessment / unit  $68,633  $71,460  $74,286

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL  1
MINUTES (MARLOMA SEWER WORKSHOP)
DECEMBER 10, 2019
   Representative from Willdan Engineering and Willdan Financial Services were
  present to further discuss the project and answer questions.

  Discussion ensued concerning the various options for moving forward with the
  project and the upfront costs associated with each of the options, including
  having the homeowners contribute to the upfront costs.

  Following discussion and comments from residents in the neighborhood, the
  CITY COUNCIL concurred that moving forward with Option 1 at an initial cost of
  $180,000 would likely be the best scenario but asked the homeowners to take it
  back to the Homeowners Association to discuss a contribution by the individual
  homeowners toward the upfront costs. Staff was directed to remain in
  communication with the homeowners and bring the matter back for consideration
  once the homeowners have had a chance to discuss a contribution toward the
  project.

4.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:25 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the City Council workshop to the regular City
Council meeting of Tuesday, December 10, 2019.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager
